# The Honest Lie: How Maps Mislead While Telling the Truth

Every map is a lie. That sounds harsh, but it's the first thing cartographers learn: a map is not the territory. A useful map is a *managed* lie—a carefully chosen set of distortions that serves a purpose. The trouble is that most of us read maps the way we read photographs, assuming they show the world as it is. In reality, every map is an argument about what matters, made by someone with a particular job to do. Understanding this doesn't make maps untrustworthy. It makes us better readers of them.
